item.title: Autonomous AI Agents for Software Development: From Code Generation to Automated Testing
item.description: This research paper presents a proposed framework for Autonomous AI Agents for Software Development, focusing on the transition from code generation to automated testing, debugging, and software verification. item.title: An evaluation guided multiagent framework for generating floor plans that comply with municipal building regulations
item.description: Abstract Generative models often produce perceptually plausible outputs that violate hard domain rules. In architectural layout generation, balancing geometric intuition with regulatory compliance remains a persistent challenge, as current frameworks routinely fail to conform to local building laws. item.description: Open source gives recipients rights to use, study, modify, and redistribute software, but language-model agents distribute behavior across code, learned parameters, prompts, tools, retrieval, configuration, and runtime state. item.description: Memory systems for persistent personal agents must move beyond isolated memories, maintaining both personal memory about whom they serve and procedural memory about how to act. item.description: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. item.title: Language modeling on tabular data: a survey of foundations, techniques and evolution
item.description: Tabular data, a prevalent data type across various domains, presents unique challenges due to its heterogeneous nature and complex structural relationships. Achieving high predictive performance and robustness in tabular data analysis holds significant promise for numerous applications. item.title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. item.title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
item.description: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on local robot manipulation, yet their success does not readily translate to long-horizon mobile manipulation. item.description: Automated generation of medical reports using AI can help speed up diagnosis and reduce doctor workload, but currently, the most efficient forms of automation use centralized training, which requires hospitals to share sensitive patient data. item.title: Fragmented control, collective risk: multi‐agent AI and the coming governance crisis
item.description: Abstract Multi‐agent artificial intelligence (MAAI) systems are increasingly deployed across economic and digital infrastructures. Existing regulatory frameworks, including the EU AI Act and related initiatives, largely focus on individual AI systems and are therefore poorly suited to govern risks that arise from agent interaction. item.title: Agentic Displacement in Second Language Writing: The Acquisitional Consequences of Delegating Writing to Autonomous AI Browsers
item.description: Autonomous AI browsers such as Perplexity Comet and Copilot Mode in Microsoft Edge can receive a writing assignment, draft a response, and submit it with little language produced by the learner.
